bitstream.command_form: one byte, high nibble the command, low nibble the argument's length in bytes, then the argument big-endian

command_meanings.6: next data's width in bits, less one
command_meanings.0 1: CRAM data follows, then two zero bytes
command_meanings.0 3: block RAM data follows, then two zero bytes
command_meanings.2: CRC-16 of the bytes since the CRC reset
command_meanings.9: option bits; bit mask 1 is icepack -s (no deep sleep)

crc.covers: bytes after the reset command, up to and including the CRC command's byte

options.no_bram: icepack -n leaves out the block RAM data commands

bitstream.tile_bit: B{r}[{c}] of a tile is CRAM bank `bank`, line line0 + layout.rows[r], position pos0 + layout.cols[c]
bitstream.ram_bit: word w, bit k of a block RAM is block RAM bank `bank`, line w, position pos0 + ram_bits[k]; .ram_data X Y names it by its ramb tile
bitstream.extra_bit: .extra_bit BANK POS LINE is CRAM bank BANK, line LINE, position POS

logic_cell.lut_index: index i = in_0 + 2 in_1 + 4 in_2 + 8 in_3: the LUT's output when the inputs are those bits

flip_flop.verilog: always @(posedge clk) if (cen) x <= sr ? 1'b0 : lout;
always @(posedge clk) if (cen) x <= sr ? 1'b1 : lout;
always @(posedge clk, posedge sr) if (sr) x <= 1'b0; else if (cen) x <= lout;
always @(posedge clk, posedge sr) if (sr) x <= 1'b1; else if (cen) x <= lout;
always @(negedge clk) if (cen) x <= sr ? 1'b0 : lout;
always @(negedge clk) if (cen) x <= sr ? 1'b1 : lout;
always @(negedge clk, posedge sr) if (sr) x <= 1'b0; else if (cen) x <= lout;
always @(negedge clk, posedge sr) if (sr) x <= 1'b1; else if (cen) x <= lout;

carry.with CarryInSet: assign co = (in_1 & in_2) | ((in_1 | in_2) & ci); assign ci = 1;

logic_cell.names: in_0..in_3 the cell's inputs, lout the LUT's output, out the cell's output, co carry out, ci the tile's carry_in_mux (the first cell's carry in), clk/cen/sr the tile's shared clock, enable and set/reset, x a net with none of these names

tile_functions.note: non-routing settings of each kind of tile, by IceStorm's names; LC_k is a logic cell's 20 bits (see logic_cell)

pins.note: package pin: the I/O tile and its PIO (z)

gbufin.note: I/O tile (x, y) whose fabout drives global network g

gbufpin.note: the pad (x, y, z) that can drive global network g

colbuf.note: column buffer at (x, y) feeds tile (x, y)

ieren.note: PIO (x, y, z) has its IE/REN bits in PIO (x, y, z)

cells.note: special-purpose cells; each port or setting is a name in a tile (a net or a configuration bit)

routing.note: a switch drives dst from one source, chosen by its bits' values (first bit first); names are the tile's own names for nets. Every tile with switches has one switch box. A net shape lists its tiles and names relative to its lowest (x, then y) tile, and is placed with that tile at every position of each rectangle [x0, x1, y0, y1]
